translation: Mind is the forerunner of mental states, mind is their chief, they are mind-made. If one speaks or acts with a corrupted mind, then suffering follows them, even as the wheel follows the hoof of the drawing ox.
literal_translation: Mental states have mind as forerunner, have mind as chief, are mind-made. If with corrupted mind one speaks or does [anything], from that [cause] suffering follows him, like a wheel [follows] the foot of the drawing [ox].

translation: Mental states are preceded by mind, have mind as their leader, and are mind-made. If one speaks or acts with a pure mind, happiness follows them like a shadow that never leaves.
literal_translation: Mental phenomena have mind as forerunner, have mind as chief, are made of mind. If, with a clear mind, one speaks or acts, because of that, happiness follows him, like a shadow not going away.

translation: “He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me.” In those who harbor such thoughts, hatred is not appeased.
literal_translation: He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he took from me; for those who bind that (grudge), hatred for them is not calmed.

translation: “He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me.” In those who do not harbor such resentment, hatred is stilled.
literal_translation: He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he brought [away] my [property]; and for those who do not bind that [on themselves], hatred is calmed for them.

translation: For never in this world is hatred stilled by hatred; it is stilled by non-hatred. This is an eternal law.
literal_translation: For never here by hatred are hatreds stilled; but by non-hatred they are stilled; this is the eternal law.

translation: Others do not understand that we must perish here. But for those who understand this, their quarrels are thereby stilled.
literal_translation: But others do not understand; we here must perish. And those who understand in that regard, from that [understanding] quarrels subside.

translation: One who dwells observing beauty, unrestrained in the senses, immoderate in eating, lazy and low in energy—Māra truly overpowers him, as the wind overthrows a weak tree.
literal_translation: One who dwells observing beauty, unrestrained in the senses, and immoderate in eating, lazy, having low energy, that one indeed Māra overpowers, as the wind a weak tree.

translation: Māra does not overcome one who lives observing the unattractive, who is well restrained in their senses, moderate in eating, faithful and energetic—just as the wind does not overcome a rocky mountain.
literal_translation: One living observing the unattractive, well-restrained in the senses, and knowing moderation in eating, faithful and having energy aroused—truly Māra does not overcome him, as the wind a rocky mountain.

translation: One who is not free from impurity, who would wear the saffron-colored robe while devoid of self-restraint and truth, is not worthy of the saffron-colored robe.
literal_translation: Not without impurity, saffron-colored, who cloth will put on, devoid of self-restraint and truth, not he saffron-colored (robe) is worthy of.

translation: But whoever has cast out impurity, is well-established in the virtues, and is endowed with self-restraint and truth, he indeed is worthy of the monk's robe.
literal_translation: And whoever [is] of [one who has] cast off impurity, well controlled in virtues, endowed with self-restraint and truth, he indeed is worthy of the monk's robe.

translation: Taking the unessential for the essential and the essential for the unessential, they do not reach the essential, ranging in the field of wrong thoughts.
literal_translation: In the essenceless, [being] ones who perceive essence; and in the essential, [being] ones who see the essenceless; they do not reach essence, [being] ones whose range is wrong intention.

translation: Knowing the essential as essential and the unessential as unessential, they reach the essence, ranging in the sphere of right intention.
literal_translation: And having known the essential as essential and the unessential as unessential, they attain the essential, [being those] having right thought as their field of activity.

translation: Just as the rain penetrates a poorly-roofed house, so lust penetrates an undeveloped mind.
literal_translation: Just as a poorly-roofed house the rain penetrates, so an undeveloped mind lust penetrates.

translation: Just as rain does not penetrate a well-thatched house, even so lust does not penetrate a well-developed mind.
literal_translation: Just as a house well-thatched, rain not penetrates; even so a well-developed mind, lust not penetrates.

translation: Here he sorrows, hereafter he sorrows; the evil-doer sorrows in both states. He sorrows, he is afflicted, seeing the impurity of his own deeds.
literal_translation: Here he sorrows, after death he sorrows, the evil-doer in both places sorrows; he sorrows, he is troubled, having seen the soiled action of himself.

translation: Here he rejoices, hereafter he rejoices; the doer of merit rejoices in both worlds. He rejoices and is jubilant, seeing the purity of his own deeds.
literal_translation: Here he rejoices, after death he rejoices; the merit-maker in both places rejoices. He rejoices, he is delighted, having seen the purity of his own action.

translation: Here he suffers remorse, after death he suffers remorse; the evil-doer suffers remorse in both cases. He suffers remorse thinking 'Evil has been done by me'; having gone to a state of misery, he suffers remorse even more.
literal_translation: Here he suffers remorse, after death he suffers remorse, the evil-doer in both places suffers remorse, 'Evil by me is done' thus he suffers remorse, more he suffers remorse having gone to a state of misery.

translation: Here he rejoices, after death he rejoices; the maker of merit rejoices in both worlds. Thinking 'I have done merit,' he rejoices; he rejoices even more when he has gone to a happy state.
literal_translation: Here he rejoices, after death he rejoices, the one who has done merit in both places rejoices; 'Merit by me [has been] done,' thus he rejoices; still more he rejoices, [having] gone [to] a good destination.

translation: Even if he recites much of the scriptures, but if a heedless man does not act accordingly, like a cowherd counting others' cows, he has no part in the ascetic life.
literal_translation: Even if much connected text speaking, not acting accordingly is a man heedless; like a cowherd cows counting of others, not a partaker of monkhood he is.

translation: Even if he recites but little of the scriptures, yet lives according to the Dhamma; having abandoned passion, aversion, and delusion, possessing perfect knowledge and a well-liberated mind, not clinging to anything in this world or the next—he shares in the fruits of the monkhood.
literal_translation: Even a little if the scriptures speaking, of the Dhamma he is a liver-according-to-the-Dhamma, passion and aversion and having abandoned delusion, perfectly knowing well-liberated-mind, not-clinging here or there or, he sharing-in of monkhood is.

translation: Heedfulness is the path to the deathless; heedlessness is the path of death. The heedful do not die; those who are heedless are as if already dead.
literal_translation: Heedfulness [is] the path to the deathless, heedlessness [is] the path of death; the heedful [ones] do not die, those who [are] heedless [are] like dead [ones].

translation: Understanding this distinctly, the wise ones, diligent in heedfulness, rejoice in heedfulness, delighting in the domain of the Noble Ones.
literal_translation: Having known this distinctly, the wise in heedfulness, rejoice in heedfulness, delighted in the domain of the Noble Ones.

translation: Those wise ones, meditative and diligent, always possessing firm persistence, attain Nibbāna, the unsurpassed security from bondage.
literal_translation: Those meditators, diligent ones, always having persistent effort, they reach Nibbāna, the wise ones, the unsurpassed security from the yoke.

translation: For one who is energetic, mindful, pure in deed, acting with care, self-controlled, living righteously, and diligent, their fame increases greatly.
literal_translation: Of the energetic, of the mindful, of the one pure in deed, of the careful doer, of the restrained, of the righteous liver, and of the diligent, fame increases greatly.

translation: By effort and heedfulness, by restraint and self-control, let the wise man make for himself an island which no flood can overwhelm.
literal_translation: By effort and by heedfulness, by restraint and by self-control, an island let the wise man make, which the flood does not overwhelm.

translation: Foolish, unwise people indulge in negligence; but the wise person guards heedfulness like their best treasure.
literal_translation: Fools, unwise people, indulge in negligence; and the wise one guards heedfulness like a best treasure.

translation: Do not indulge in heedlessness, nor in intimacy with sensual delight; for the heedful one, meditating, attains vast happiness.
literal_translation: Do not engage in negligence, do not engage in intimacy with delight in sensual pleasure; for the diligent one meditating, attains vast happiness.

translation: When the wise person drives away negligence through diligence, having ascended the palace of wisdom, sorrowless, he looks down upon the sorrowing people; just as one standing on a mountain looks down upon those standing on the ground, the wise one looks down upon the fools.
literal_translation: When the sage drives away negligence by diligence, having climbed the tower of wisdom, sorrowless, he looks at the sorrowful people; as one standing on a mountain looks at those standing on the ground, the wise man looks at the fools.

translation: Diligent among the heedless, wide awake among those asleep, the wise one moves forward like a swift horse leaving behind a weak one.
literal_translation: Diligent among the heedless, much-awake among those asleep, like a swift horse having left behind a weak horse, the wise one goes.

translation: By diligence, Maghavā reached the highest state among the gods. The wise praise diligence; heedlessness is always blamed.
literal_translation: By means of diligence, Maghavant went to pre-eminence of the gods; they praise diligence; heedlessness is blamed always.

translation: A monk who delights in diligence and sees danger in negligence moves along like a fire, burning up every fetter, whether small or large.
literal_translation: A monk delighting in non-heedlessness, or seeing danger in heedlessness, burning a fetter, subtle (and) gross, goes like a fire.

translation: A monk who delights in diligence and sees danger in negligence is incapable of falling away; he is right in the presence of Nibbāna.
literal_translation: A monk delighting in diligence, or seeing danger in negligence, is incapable of decline, indeed in the vicinity of Nibbāna.

translation: The wise man makes straight the trembling, fickle mind, which is difficult to guard and hard to restrain, just as a fletcher straightens an arrow.
literal_translation: The trembling, fickle mind, hard to protect, difficult to restrain, the wise man makes straight, like a fletcher [straightens] an arrow-shaft.

translation: Like a fish thrown onto dry land, pulled out from its watery home, this mind flops about in order to escape the realm of Māra.
literal_translation: Like a fish thrown on dry land, pulled out from its watery home, this mind flops about to give up the realm of Māra.

translation: Control of the mind—which is difficult to restrain, swift, and landing wherever it wants—is good. A tamed mind brings happiness.
literal_translation: Of [the mind] hard to restrain, swift, landing wherever it wants, of the mind control is good. The mind tamed brings happiness.

translation: Extremely difficult to see, very subtle, and landing wherever it likes: the wise man should guard the mind. A guarded mind brings happiness.
literal_translation: Extremely difficult to see, very subtle, landing wherever it wants: the wise person should guard the mind; the guarded mind is a bringer of happiness.

translation: Those who restrain the mind—which travels far, wanders alone, is bodiless, and lies hidden in the heart—will be freed from the bond of Māra.
literal_translation: Those who will restrain the mind, far-ranging, wandering alone, bodiless, dwelling in the cave [of the heart], will be freed from the bond of Māra.

translation: Wisdom does not become full for one whose mind is unstable, who does not know the true Teaching, and whose confidence wavers.
literal_translation: Of one with an unstable mind, of one not knowing the true doctrine, of one whose faith is wavering, wisdom does not fully mature.

translation: For one whose mind is free of lust, whose mind is unruffled, who has transcended both merit and evil—for such a wakeful one, there is no fear.
literal_translation: For one whose mind is not oozing, whose mind is not ruffed, who has abandoned merit and evil—there is no fear for the one awake.

translation: Realizing that this body is as fragile as a clay pot and fortifying this mind like a fortress, one should attack Mara with the weapon of wisdom; one should protect what has been won and remain without attachment.
literal_translation: Having known this body to be like a clay pot, having established this mind like a fortress, one should fight Mara with the weapon of wisdom; and one should protect what is conquered, one should be without clinging.

translation: Before long, alas, this body will lie upon the earth, cast aside, devoid of consciousness, like a useless log.
literal_translation: Soon indeed this body upon the earth will lie, thrown away, devoid of consciousness, like a useless piece of wood.

translation: Whatever harm an enemy may do to an enemy, or a hater to a hater, a wrongly directed mind can do one even greater harm than that.
literal_translation: Whatever an enemy might do to an enemy, or a hostile person to a hostile person; a wrongly directed mind might make one worse than that.

translation: Neither mother nor father, nor any other relative, can do one as much good as a well-directed mind.
literal_translation: Neither mother nor father could do that, nor even other relatives; a well-directed mind could do for him even better than that.

translation: Who will investigate this earth and this world of Yama with its gods? Who will investigate the well-taught verse of Dhamma, just as a skilled person plucks a flower?
literal_translation: Who this earth will investigate, and this Yama-world together with gods? Who the well-taught Dhamma-verse, as a skilled [one] like a flower will pluck?

translation: The trainee will understand this earth and the world of Yama with its gods; the trainee will understand the well-taught verse of the Dhamma, just as a skilled person picks a flower.
literal_translation: The trainee will investigate the earth and this Yama-world including the devas; the trainee will pick the well-taught Dhamma-verse, like a skilled person picks a flower.

translation: Knowing this body to be like foam, realizing its mirage-like nature, cutting off the flower-tipped arrows of Mara, one should go where the King of Death cannot see.
literal_translation: Having known this body [to be] foam-like, fully understanding [it as having] mirage-nature, having cut the flower-arrows of Mara, one should go to the not-seeing of the King of Death.

translation: Death carries off the man who is only picking flowers, whose mind is obsessed, just as a great flood carries off a sleeping village.
literal_translation: Picking flowers indeed, a man with an attached mind, death, taking [him], goes, like a great flood [taking] a sleeping village.

translation: Death brings under its power the person who is picking flowers, whose mind is attached to them, and who is never satisfied with sensual pleasures.
literal_translation: The Ender brings under his control the man indeed picking flowers, with an attached mind, even unsatisfied in sensual pleasures.

translation: Just as a bee takes the nectar and flies away without harming the flower's beauty and fragrance, so should the sage move through the village.
literal_translation: Just as a bee, taking the nectar, goes away without harming the flower, its beauty and its fragrance, thus in the village the sage should move.

translation: Not the faults of others, not what others have done or left undone; one should consider only what oneself has done and left undone.
literal_translation: Not of others the disagreeable things, not of others what is done and not done; only of oneself one should consider things done and things not done.

translation: Just like a beautiful flower that is colorful but scentless, even so, well-spoken words are fruitless for one who does not act on them.
literal_translation: Just as a beautiful flower, having color [but] without scent, even so well-spoken speech is fruitless it is for one not doing.

translation: Just like a beautiful flower, which has color and is fragrant, so well-spoken words are fruitful for one who acts.
literal_translation: Just as a beautiful flower, having color [and] having fragrance, thus well-spoken speech is fruitful for one who is doing.

translation: Just as from a heap of flowers many garlands can be made, so by a mortal once born, much good should be done.
literal_translation: Just as from a heap of flowers one might make many garlands, thus by a born mortal should be done much good.

translation: The fragrance of flowers does not travel against the wind, nor does that of sandalwood, tagara, or jasmine. But the fragrance of the virtuous does travel against the wind; the good man wafts in all directions.
literal_translation: The fragrance of flowers does not go against the wind, nor sandalwood, nor tagara and jasmine; but the fragrance of the virtuous goes against the wind; a good man wafts unto all directions.

translation: Sandalwood, tagara, blue water lily, or even Arabian jasmine—of these varieties of fragrance, the fragrance of virtue is supreme.
literal_translation: Sandalwood, tagara flower, or even blue water lily, then Arabian jasmine; of these kinds of perfume, the fragrance of virtue is unsurpassed.

translation: This scent of jasmine and sandalwood is slight; but the scent of the virtuous is supreme, wafting even among the gods.
literal_translation: Small is this scent, which is this tagara and sandalwood; but the scent of the virtuous wafts among the gods, supreme.

translation: Mara does not find the path of those who are perfect in virtue, who dwell in heedfulness, and who are liberated through perfect knowledge.
literal_translation: Of those perfect in virtue, dwelling in heedfulness, liberated through perfect knowledge, Mara does not find the path.

translation: Just as in a heap of rubbish discarded on the high road, a sweet-smelling and delightful lotus might grow there.
literal_translation: Just as in a rubbish-place, discarded on a main road, a lotus there might grow, sweet-smelling, mind-pleasing.

translation: Thus, among those who have become like rubbish, among the ordinary people who are blinded by ignorance, the disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened Buddha outshines them with wisdom.
literal_translation: Thus, in those become like rubbish, in the ordinary person become blind, the disciple of the Perfectly Awakened One outshines by wisdom.

translation: Long is the night to one who is awake; long is the league to one who is tired; long is the round of rebirths for fools who do not know the True Teaching.
literal_translation: Long [is] the night of the one being awake; long [is] the league of the tired one; long [is] the wandering-on of fools not knowing the True Teaching.

translation: If, while wandering, one does not find a companion better than or equal to oneself, one should firmly resolve to live alone; there is no friendship with a fool.
literal_translation: If, wandering, one should not find a better [one or] one similar to oneself, one should do solitary wandering firmly; there is no companionship in a fool.

translation: 'I have sons, I have wealth,' thus the fool troubles himself. Since even his own self is not his own, how can he have sons or wealth?
literal_translation: 'Sons are for me, wealth is for me,' thus the fool suffers. Since the self indeed is not for the self, from where are sons, from where is wealth?

translation: The fool who knows his foolishness is wise at least to that extent, but the fool who thinks himself wise is called a fool indeed.
literal_translation: Whoever being a fool knows his foolishness, he is wise by that; but the fool who imagines himself wise, he is truly called 'a fool'.

translation: Even if for his whole life a fool associates with a wise man, he does not understand the Dhamma, just as a spoon does not know the taste of the soup.
literal_translation: Even if for as long as life lasts a fool closely attends to a wise man, he does not comprehend the teaching, like a spoon the taste of soup.

translation: If even for a moment a wise person associates with a sage, they quickly understand the Dhamma, just as the tongue tastes the flavor of the soup.
literal_translation: If even for a moment a wise person associates with a wise man, quickly they comprehend the Teaching, like the tongue the taste of soup.

translation: Fools of poor wisdom practice [life] with themselves as if with an enemy, doing evil deeds which have bitter results.
literal_translation: Fools, the unwise ones, wander with [their own] self just like with an enemy, performing evil action which is of bitter fruit.

translation: That deed is not well done which, after doing it, one regrets, and the consequences of which one reaps with a tearful face and weeping.
literal_translation: That action done is not good, which having done one regrets, [and] whose result one experiences crying [with] a tear-stained face.

translation: But that deed is well done which, after doing it, one does not regret, and whose result one experiences with a satisfied and happy mind.
literal_translation: But that deed [is] done well, which having done [one] does not regret, of which [one] satisfied [and] happy-minded, experiences the result.

translation: The fool thinks it is sweet as honey as long as the evil deed does not ripen; but when the evil deed ripens, the fool undergoes suffering.
literal_translation: A fool thinks it is sweet as honey as long as evil does not ripen; but when the evil ripens, the fool undergoes suffering.

translation: Month after month, even if a fool should eat his food with the tip of a blade of kusa grass, he is not worth a sixteenth part of those who have comprehended the Dhamma.
literal_translation: Month by month, with the tip of kusa [grass], a fool might eat food; he is not worth a sixteenth part of those who have comprehended the Dhamma.

translation: An evil deed that has been done does not certainly curdle at once, like milk. It follows the fool, smoldering, like fire covered by ashes.
literal_translation: For an evil action having been done does not instantly turn like milk; it follows the fool burning, like fire covered with ashes.

translation: Knowledge arises for a fool only to his own harm; it destroys the fool's good fortune, splitting apart his head.
literal_translation: Only for harm knowledge for a fool arises; it harms of the fool the bright portion, of him the head splitting apart.

translation: He might wish for unwarranted status, precedence among the monks, authority in the monasteries, and homage from other families.
literal_translation: He might wish for unwarranted status, and precedence among the monks, and authority in the monasteries, homage in other families and.

translation: “Let both laypeople and monastics think that this was done by me alone; let them be under my control alone in all duties, whatever they may be.” Such is the fool’s intention; his desire and pride increase.
literal_translation: “By me alone something done let them think, householders and monastics both; under my control alone let them be, in duties and non-duties in anything”; thus of the fool the intention, desire and pride increase.

translation: One is the way to material gain, another is the way to Nibbāna. Having clearly understood this, a monk, a disciple of the Buddha, should not delight in worldly honor but should foster seclusion.
literal_translation: For one (is) the cause for gain, another (is) leading to Nibbāna; having understood this thus, a monk, a disciple of the Buddha, should not delight in honor, he should foster seclusion.

translation: One should follow a wise person who reproves and points out faults, as if they were a pointer out of hidden treasures. For one who follows such a person, it is better, not worse.
literal_translation: Like a proclaimer of treasures, whom one should see as a fault-seer, a reprover, an intelligent man—such a sage one should associate with. For one associating with such a one, better it becomes, not worse.

translation: One should advise, one should instruct, and one should restrain from bad manners; for such a person is dear to the virtuous and undear to the unvirtuous.
literal_translation: One should advise and one should instruct, and from impoliteness one should restrain; for he is dear to the virtuous, he is undear to the unvirtuous.

translation: One should not associate with bad friends, nor with the lowest of men. One should associate with good friends, and with the best of men.
literal_translation: Not should associate with bad friends, not should associate with worst men; should associate with good friends, should associate with highest men.

translation: He who drinks the Dhamma dwells happily with a serene mind; the wise man always delights in the Dhamma proclaimed by the Noble One.
literal_translation: One drinking the Dhamma happily dwells with a serene mind; the wise man always delights in the Dhamma proclaimed by the Noble One.

translation: Irregators lead the water, fletchers bend the arrow, carpenters shape the wood, and the wise tame themselves.
literal_translation: Irrigators indeed lead the water, arrow-makers bend the arrow-shaft, carpenters bend the wood, the wise tame the self.

translation: Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, so the wise are not moved by blame and praise.
literal_translation: A rock just as solid, by the wind not is shaken, thus amidst blame and praise, not move the wise.

translation: Just as a deep pool is clear and undisturbed, so the wise, having heard the teachings, become serene.
literal_translation: Just as a pool [is] deep, clear, [and] undisturbed; thus, having heard the teachings, the wise become serene.

translation: Everywhere indeed the virtuous give up attachment; the good do not chatter with a desire for sensual pleasures. Whether touched by happiness or by pain, the wise display no elation or depression.
literal_translation: Everywhere indeed virtuous men give up [attachment]; virtuous ones not desiring sensual pleasure do not chatter. Touched by happiness or indeed by pain, the wise do not display high and low [fluctuation].

translation: Neither for one's own sake nor for the sake of another, should one desire a son, wealth, or a kingdom; nor should one desire one's own success by unjust means. Such a person is virtuous, wise, and righteous.
literal_translation: Not for the sake of self, not for the sake of another, he should not wish for a son, not wealth, not a kingdom; he should not wish for his own success by unrighteousness; he would be virtuous, wise, and righteous.

translation: Few are those among men who reach the far shore; the rest of mankind only runs up and down along the bank.
literal_translation: Few are those among humans, which people are goers to the far shore; but this other mankind only runs along the bank.

translation: But those who follow the Dhamma in the Dhamma well-taught, those people will reach the far shore, across the realm of death which is so difficult to cross.
literal_translation: And indeed whoever in the well-taught teaching are followers of the teaching, those people will go to the far shore, across the realm of death extremely difficult to cross.

translation: Abandoning the dark state, the wise man should develop the bright. Having gone from home to homelessness, in seclusion where it is difficult to find delight...
literal_translation: Having completely abandoned the dark state, the wise man should develop the bright; having come to homelessness from home, in seclusion where it is hard to delight.

translation: There he should seek delight, having abandoned sensual pleasures and possessing nothing; the wise man should cleanse himself from the defilements of the mind.
literal_translation: There delight he should desire, having abandoned sensual pleasures, being without possessions, he should cleanse himself from mental defilements, the wise man.

translation: Those whose minds are well cultivated in the factors of enlightenment, who delight in relinquishing attachment without grasping, they—radiant ones with effluents destroyed—attain final Nibbāna in the world.
literal_translation: Of whom in the elements of full awakening the mind is thoroughly well cultivated, in the relinquishing of grasping, not holding onto, who are delighted, with effluents exhausted, the radiant ones, they in the world are completely quenched.

translation: For one who has completed the journey, who is free from sorrow, who is released in every way, and who has abandoned all bonds, no fever of passion is found.
literal_translation: Of the one whose journey is finished, the one without grief, the one freed everywhere, the one whose all bonds are abandoned, distress does not exist.

translation: The mindful depart; they do not delight in a home. Just as swans leave their pond, they abandon every abode.
literal_translation: The mindful ones set out; they do not delight in a home. Like swans having left a pond, they abandon home after home.

translation: Those who have no accumulation, who have fully understood the fuel of existence, whose domain is the void and the signless liberation—their track, like that of birds in the sky, is hard to trace.
literal_translation: Of whom accumulation there is not, who have fully understood food, for whom void and signless liberation is the domain, like the birds in the sky, their track is hard to follow.

translation: One whose defilements are exhausted, who is not dependent on food, whose range is the liberation of emptiness and the signless—their track is hard to trace, like that of birds in the sky.
literal_translation: Of whom the outflows are exhausted, and in food not dependent, emptiness and signless and liberation of whom [is] the range, like of birds in the sky, the path of him [is] difficult to follow.

translation: Even the gods envy him whose senses are stilled like horses well tamed by a trainer, who has abandoned conceit and is free from taints.
literal_translation: Of whom the senses are stilled, like horses well tamed by a trainer, of the one with conceit abandoned, of the taintless one, even the gods envy that such a one.

translation: Like the earth, he is not opposed; like a gatepost is such a person of good vows; like a lake free from mud, for such a one there are no more rebirths.
literal_translation: Like earth not is opposed, gatepost-like such well-vowed [person], lake-like free-from-mud, rebirths not exist of such a one.

translation: His mind is calm, calm are his speech and action, of one who is liberated by perfect knowledge, who is tranquil and unaffected.
literal_translation: Calm is his mind, calm are his speech and action, of the one liberated through perfect knowledge, of the calmed one, of such a character.

translation: The man who is not credulous, who knows the uncreated, who has broken the connection to rebirth, who has destroyed all opportunity for further existence, and who has given up all desire—he is indeed a supreme person.
literal_translation: The man who (is) not credulous, a knower of the uncreated, and a connection-breaker, and whatever man (is) one whose opportunity is destroyed, whose desire is given up, he indeed (is) a supreme person.

translation: Whether in a village or in a forest, whether in a valley or on high ground—wherever Arahants dwell, that place is delightful.
literal_translation: In a village or whether in a forest, in a valley or whether on high ground, wherever Arahants dwell, that is a delightful place.

translation: Delightful are the forests where ordinary people find no delight. Those free from passion will find delight there, for they are not seekers of sensual pleasure.
literal_translation: Beautiful are the forests, where the person does not delight; those free from passion will delight, they are not seekers of sensual pleasure.

translation: Even a thousand words, if they are composed of meaningless lines, are not as good as a single meaningful word, which, having been heard, brings peace.
literal_translation: Even a thousand [words] if words [are] connected with meaningless lines, one meaningful line [is] better, which having heard [one] is calmed.

translation: Even if there are a thousand verses composed of unbeneficial lines, one line of verse is better, hearing which one is calmed.
literal_translation: Even if [there be] a thousand verses composed of unbeneficial words, one verse-line [is] better, which having heard, [one] is calmed.

translation: And though one should recite a hundred verses composed of unbeneficial lines, one word of the teaching is better, which having heard, one is calmed.
literal_translation: And whoever should recite a hundred verses connected with unbeneficial sayings, one word of the Dhamma is better, having heard which, one is calmed.

translation: Though one should conquer a million men in battle, yet he who conquers himself is the supreme victor in battle.
literal_translation: Whoever should conquer a thousand by a thousand men in battle, and should conquer one—himself—he indeed is the supreme victor in battle.

translation: Though one should conquer a million men in battle, yet he who conquers himself is the supreme victor in battle. Victory over oneself is truly better than victory over all other people, for a person who is self-controlled and always lives with self-restraint.
literal_translation: Whoever should conquer a thousand by a thousand men in battle, and should conquer one—himself—he indeed is the supreme victor in battle. Self truly conquered [is] better than this other offspring; for a person of self-tamed [one], always of [one] acting with self-control.

translation: Victory over oneself is truly better than victory over all other people, for a person who is self-controlled and always lives with self-restraint.
literal_translation: Self truly conquered [is] better than this other offspring; for a person of self-tamed [one], always of [one] acting with self-control.

translation: Victory over oneself is truly better than victory over all other people, for a person who is self-controlled and always lives with self-restraint. Neither a god, nor a gandhabbo, nor Māra together with Brahma, can turn into defeat the victory of such a person who has self-mastery.
literal_translation: Self truly conquered [is] better than this other offspring; for a person of self-tamed [one], always of [one] acting with self-control. Neither a god nor a heavenly musician, nor Māra with Brahma, could make into a defeat the victory of such a person.

translation: Neither a god, nor a gandhabbo, nor Māra together with Brahma, can turn into defeat the victory of such a person who has self-mastery.
literal_translation: Neither a god nor a heavenly musician, nor Māra with Brahma, could make into a defeat the victory of such a person.

translation: Month after month for a hundred years, one might perform sacrifices costing a thousand units each. But if one were to honor, even for a moment, a person who has developed themselves, that single act of honoring is far better than a hundred years of ritual sacrifice.
literal_translation: Month after month with a thousand, whoever would sacrifice for a hundred years; but if one would honor for even a moment one who has developed their self; just that honoring is better than a hundred years of offering.

translation: Though a person should tend the sacrificial fire in the forest for a hundred years, if they were to honour even for a moment one who has developed themselves, that honouring is indeed better than a hundred years of sacrifice.
literal_translation: Whoever and for a hundred years, a person, fire should worship in forest, and one self-developed person even for a moment should honour; that very honouring is better than if a hundred years of sacrifice.

translation: Whatever offering or sacrifice one might make in the world for a whole year, seeking merit, all of that is not worth even a quarter of the merit gained by paying respect to the upright ones, which is far better.
literal_translation: Whatever offering or sacrifice in the world for a year one might sacrifice seeking merit, all even that not a fourth part goes; paying respect among the upright is better.

translation: For one who is habitually respectful, who always honors the seniors, four qualities increase: long life, beauty, happiness, and strength.
literal_translation: For one of the nature of bowing down, always honoring the elderly, four things increase: life, complexion, happiness, strength.

translation: And though one should live a hundred years, unethical and unconcentrated, yet better is a single day's life of one who is virtuous and meditative.
literal_translation: And whoever should live for a hundred years, unprincipled, uncomposed, life for one day [is] better for the virtuous meditator.

translation: And whoever should live for a hundred years, foolish and unconcentrated, better is the life of a single day for one who is wise and meditative.
literal_translation: And who should live for a hundred years, foolish, uncomposed; better is the life for one day of the wise, of the meditator.

translation:
And who for a hundred years might live,
Lazy and of low energy,
Better is the life of a single day,
For one who arouses effort firmly.
literal_translation: And whoever for a hundred years should live, lazy, lacking in energy, for one day life is better of one firmly arousing energy.

translation: And whoever should live for a hundred years not seeing the rising and falling of things, better is the life of a single day for one who sees their rising and falling.
literal_translation: And whoever for a hundred years should live not seeing rising and falling, better is life for a single day of one seeing rising and falling.

translation: And whoever should live a hundred years, not seeing the deathless state; yet better is the life of a single day for one who sees the deathless state.
literal_translation: And whoever should live for a hundred years not seeing the deathless state, better is the living for a single day of one seeing the deathless state.

translation: Though one should live a hundred years not seeing the supreme Dhamma, yet better is the life of a single day for one who sees the supreme Dhamma.
literal_translation: Whoever and a hundred years should live not seeing the supreme Dhamma, life for one day is better for one seeing the supreme Dhamma.

translation: One should hasten to do good and restrain the mind from evil; for the mind of one who is slow in doing merit delights in evil.
literal_translation: One should hasten in goodness, one should restrain the mind from evil; for of one doing merit slowly, the mind delights in evil.

translation: If a man should do evil, let him not do it again and again. Let him not find pleasure in it, for the accumulation of evil is painful.
literal_translation: If a man should do evil action, he should not do it again and again; he should not make desire in that; painful is the accumulation of evil action.

translation: If a person should do merit, they should do it again and again. They should find delight in it; happy is the accumulation of merit.
literal_translation: If a man should do merit, he should do that again and again, in that he should make desire; happy is the accumulation of merit.

translation: Even an evildoer encounters good fortune as long as their evil deed does not ripen. But when the evil deed ripens, then the evildoer experiences the evil consequences.
literal_translation: Even an evildoer sees good so long as the evil matures not; but when the evil matures, then the evildoer sees evils.

translation: Even a good person encounters evil as long as the good deed does not ripen; but when the good deed ripens, then the good person encounters good things.
literal_translation: Even a good person sees evil as long as the good (deed) does not ripen, but when the good (deed) ripens, then the good person sees good (things).

translation: Do not think lightly of evil, saying, 'It will not come to me.' Even a water jar is filled by the falling of water drops. Likewise, the fool, gathering it little by little, is filled with evil.
literal_translation: May one not think lightly of evil: 'To me that will not come.' By the falling of a water drop, even a water jar is filled. The fool is filled with evil, accumulating it even a little by little.

translation: One should not think lightly of merit, saying, 'It will not come to me.' Even a water jar is filled by the falling of drops of water. A wise man is filled with merit, accumulating it little by little.
literal_translation: May one not disregard merit, [thinking] 'that will not come to me.' By the falling of water-drops even a water jar is filled; the wise man is filled with merit, even a little by a little gathering.

translation: Just as a wealthy merchant with only a small caravan avoids a dangerous road, and just as one who loves life avoids poison, so should one avoid evil deeds.
literal_translation: Like a merchant a dangerous road, having a small caravan, having great wealth, like one wishing to live poison, evils one should avoid.

translation: If there is no wound on the hand, one could carry poison in the hand. Poison does not affect the woundless; there is no evil for one who does no evil.
literal_translation: If in the hand there would not be a wound, one would carry poison with the hand; poison does not follow the woundless one; there is no evil for one not doing [evil].

translation: Whoever offends an innocent person, a man who is pure and unblemished, the evil recoils upon that very fool, like fine dust thrown against the wind.
literal_translation: Whoever offends an innocent man, a pure person, an unblemished one, that evil returns to that very fool, like fine dust thrown against the wind.

translation: Some are reborn in a womb, evil-doers in hell, the righteous go to heaven, and the taintless attain final emancipation.
literal_translation: Some are born in a womb; the evil-doers [go to] hell; the fortunate ones go to heaven; the taintless ones attain parinibbāna.

translation: Neither in the sky nor in the middle of the sea, nor by entering a mountain cleft, is there found any place on earth where, staying there, one might be freed from the consequences of an evil deed.
literal_translation: Not in the sky, not in the middle of the sea, not having entered a mountain crevice; that place on earth does not exist, where standing, one might be released from an evil action.

translation: Neither in the sky nor in the middle of the sea, nor by entering a mountain cleft—there exists no place on earth where one might stand and death would not overcome them.
literal_translation: Not in the sky, not in the middle of the sea, not having entered a mountain cleft; that place on earth is not found, where standing, death would not overcome [one].

translation: All tremble at the stick, all fear death. Having made oneself the example, one should neither kill nor cause to kill.
literal_translation: All tremble at the stick, all fear death; having made oneself the example, one should not kill, one should not cause to kill.

translation: All tremble at the rod, life is dear to all; having made oneself the example, one should neither kill nor cause to kill.
literal_translation: All tremble of the stick, to all life is dear, having made self the example, one should not strike, one should not cause to slaughter.

translation: Whoever harms with a stick living beings who desire happiness, while seeking his own happiness, does not obtain happiness after death.
literal_translation: Living beings desiring happiness, whoever with a stick harms, for himself happiness seeking, having gone forward (after death) he not gets happiness.

translation: One who does not harm with a stick living beings who desire happiness, while seeking happiness for oneself, after death that one obtains happiness.
literal_translation: Living beings [who are] desiring happiness, who with a stick does not harm, seeking happiness of oneself, having gone forth (after death) he obtains happiness.

translation: Do not speak harshly to anyone; those spoken to might retort to you. For quarrelsome speech is painful, and retaliations might strike you.
literal_translation: Do not say anything harsh to anyone; those spoken to might retort to you; for quarrelsome speech is painful; retaliations might touch you.

translation: If you do not stir yourself up, like a broken bronze gong, then you have reached Nibbana; no agitation is found in you.
literal_translation: If you do not agitate yourself, as a broken bronze gong, this [one] you are reached Nibbana; agitation for you is not found.

translation: Just as a cowherd drives cows to pasture with a stick, so old age and death drive the life of living beings.
literal_translation: Just as with a stick a cowherd drives cows to pasture, so old age and death drive the life of living beings.

translation: But when the fool performs evil deeds, he does not realize it; through his own deeds the unwise person is tormented, just like one burned by fire.
literal_translation: But doing evil deeds the fool does not understand; by his own deeds the unwise one is tormented even as [one] burned by fire.

translation: Whoever wrongs the unarmed and innocent with a stick, they very quickly undergo one of ten states.
literal_translation: Whoever with a stick against those without sticks, against the non-corrupt, wrongs, one of ten thing[s] very quickly he undergoes.

translation: He might experience severe pain, loss of wealth, bodily injury, a serious illness, or mental derangement.
literal_translation: Severe pain, loss, and breaking of the body, or even a serious affliction, and mental derangement he would experience.

translation: Or trouble from the king, and a harsh false accusation, and the loss of relatives, and the destruction of wealth.
literal_translation: Or trouble from a king, and a brutal slandering, and a depletion of relatives, and a breaking of possessions.

translation: Then, or fire—the bright one—burns his houses; upon the breakup of the body, the fool is reborn in hell.
literal_translation: Then or his houses fire burns, the bright one; at the breakup of the body, the witless one is reborn in hell.

translation: Neither nudity nor matted hair nor smearing with mud, nor fasting nor sleeping on the bare ground, nor dust and dirt nor the practice of squatting, can purify a mortal who has not overcome doubt.
literal_translation: Neither naked-conduct nor dreadlocks nor mud, nor fasting nor sleeping on the ground or dust-dirt and squatting-exertion, purify a mortal who has not overcome doubt.

translation: Even if dressed up, if one should live in a balanced manner—tranquil, tamed, restrained, a spiritual practitioner—having laid aside violence towards all beings, he is a holy man, he is an ascetic, he is a monk.
literal_translation: Even if decorated, if he should live equally, peaceful, tamed, restrained, a spiritual practitioner, having put down the stick towards all beings, that one (is) a Brahman, that one (is) an ascetic, that (one is) a monk.

translation: Is there any man in the world, restrained by conscience, who avoids reproach, just as a noble horse avoids the whip?
literal_translation: A man restrained by conscience, any in the world is found, who avoids reproach, like a noble horse a whip.

translation: Like a noble horse touched by the whip, be ardent and urgent. By faith, virtue, effort, stillness, and investigation of reality, being accomplished in wisdom and conduct and mindful, you will abandon this great suffering.
literal_translation: A horse like a noble one touched by the whip, ardent and urgent be you all; by faith, by virtue and by effort and, by stillness, by investigation of reality and, accomplished in wisdom and conduct, mindful, you will give up this great suffering.

translation: Indeed, irrigators lead the water; fletchers straighten the arrow; carpenters shape the wood; the virtuous tame themselves.
literal_translation: Certainly irrigators lead the water, fletchers bend the arrow-shaft, carpenters bend the wood, the virtuous ones tame the self.

translation: How can there be laughter, how can there be joy, when the world is constantly burning? Shrouded in darkness, why do you not seek a light?
literal_translation: What is the laughter, what is the joy, while it is constantly burning? Enveloped by darkness, you do not seek a lamp.

translation: Look at this adorned image, a mass of sores propped up, sickly, full of many plans, which has no permanent stability.
literal_translation: See the mind-made image, a collection of wounds raised up, sick, having many intentions, of which there is no stable standing.

translation: This body is worn out, a fragile nest of disease; this putrid mass breaks up, for life ends in death.
literal_translation: This form is worn out, a nest of disease, fragile; the rotting body breaks up, for life has death as its end.

translation: These bones, thrown away like bottle gourds in autumn, are dove-gray; having seen them, what delight is there?
literal_translation: Whichever these [are] thrown away, like bottle gourds in autumn, dove-gray bones; those having seen, what delight [is there]?

translation: A city is built of bones, plastered with flesh and blood; within it dwell old age and death, pride and denigration.
literal_translation: A city made of bones, with a plastering of flesh and blood, where old age and death, conceit and denigration are deposited.

translation: Indeed, even the beautifully adorned royal chariots wear out, and the body too reaches old age; but the Dhamma of the virtuous does not grow old—thus do the virtuous truly proclaim to the virtuous.
literal_translation: Truly royal chariots well-adorned wear out, and also the body reaches old age, and the teaching of the virtuous not reaches old age, the virtuous truly to the virtuous proclaim.

translation: This man of little learning grows old like an ox; his flesh increases, but his wisdom does not.
literal_translation: This unlearned man ages like an ox; the flesh of him grows, the wisdom of him not grows.

translation: I have wandered through the cycle of many births, searching for the house-builder but not finding him; painful is birth again and again.
literal_translation: Through the wandering of many births I wandered, not finding [him], the house-builder seeking; painful is birth again and again.

translation: O house-builder, you are seen! You will not build a house again. All your rafters are broken, the ridge-pole is deconstructed. The mind has gone to the unconditioned; it has reached the destruction of cravings.
literal_translation: O house-builder, you are seen; again a house you will not make; all your rafters are broken, the ridge-pole is deconstructed; the mind is gone to the unconstructed; it reached the exhaustion of cravings.

translation: They who have not led the holy life, and have not gained wealth in their youth, pine away like old herons in a pond without fish.
literal_translation: Having not led the holy life, having not gained wealth in youth, they brood like old herons in a pond depleted of fish.

translation: Neither having lived the spiritual life nor having gained wealth in their youth, they lie like spent arrows shot from a bow, sighing over the past.
literal_translation: Having not lived the spiritual life, having not obtained wealth in youth, they lie like arrows shot from a bow, lamenting past things.

translation: If one holds oneself dear, one should protect oneself well. During any one of the three stages of life, a wise man should keep watch.
literal_translation: If one should know oneself as dear, one should protect him well-guarded; during one of the three stages of life, the wise man should keep watch.

translation: First, one should establish oneself in what is proper, and then one should instruct others; thus the wise man would not be stained.
literal_translation: First one should establish oneself in what is proper; then one should instruct others; the wise man would not be stained.

translation: If one would act towards oneself just as one instructs another, then, being well-tamed, one could tame others; for the self is indeed difficult to tame.
literal_translation: Oneself if so should-do, just as another [one] instructs, well-tamed indeed [one] would-tame; self for truly difficult-to-tame.

translation: One is indeed one's own protector; for who else could the protector be? With a self well-controlled, one obtains a protector that is difficult to find.
literal_translation: Self indeed is the protector of self; who indeed could be another protector? By the self indeed well-controlled, one obtains a protector difficult to find.

translation: Truly, the evil done by oneself, born of oneself, and produced by oneself, crushes the unwise one, just as a diamond crushes a stone-made jewel.
literal_translation: By oneself indeed [the] done evil, self-born, self-produced, crushes [the] unwise [one], [as] a diamond a stone-made jewel.

translation: One whose extreme immorality is spread over him like a maluva creeper over a sal tree, he does to himself exactly what his enemy would wish for him.
literal_translation: For whom extreme bad behavior, like a maluva creeper spread over a sal tree, he makes himself so, just as an enemy wishes for him.

translation: Bad deeds and things harmful to oneself are easily done; what is beneficial and good is truly hardest to do.
literal_translation: Bad things and unbeneficial things of oneself (are) easy to do; whatever indeed (is) beneficial and good, that indeed (is) extremely difficult to do.

translation: Whatever foolish person, relying on an evil view, disdains the teaching of the Arahants—the Noble Ones who live righteously—he bears fruit only for his own destruction, just as the bamboo bears fruit to its own end.
literal_translation: Whoever foolish person, having depended on an evil view, rejects the teaching of the Arahants, the Noble Ones living the Dhamma, he bears fruit for self-destruction, like the fruit of the bamboo.

translation: For by oneself is evil done, by oneself is one defiled; by oneself is evil left undone, by oneself alone is one purified. Purity and impurity depend on oneself; no one can purify another.
literal_translation: Indeed by oneself evil is done, by oneself one is defiled, by oneself evil is not done, by oneself only one is purified, purity and impurity are individual; another person cannot purify another person.

translation: One should not neglect one's own welfare for the sake of another's, however great. Having understood one's own welfare, one should be intent on one's own goal.
literal_translation: One's own welfare [for the sake of] another's welfare, even by much one should not neglect. Having directly known one's own welfare, one should be intent on one's own benefit.

translation: One should not follow low teachings; one should not live with negligence. One should not follow wrong views, and one should not be a prolonger of the world.
literal_translation: A low teaching one should not follow, with negligence one should not live, a wrong view one should not follow, not should one be a world-increaser.

translation: One should get up and not be negligent. One should practice the Dhamma well. One who practices the Dhamma sleeps happily, in this world and in the next.
literal_translation: One should stand up, one should not be negligent; one should practice the teaching well-practiced; a Dhamma-practitioner sleeps happily, in this world and in the next.

translation: One should practice the Dhamma well; one should not practice it badly. He who lives by the Dhamma lives happily in this world and the next.
literal_translation: One should practice the Dhamma well-conducted, one should not practice it ill-conducted; he who lives the Dhamma lives happily in this world and in the next.

translation: As one would see a bubble, as one would see a mirage; so the King of Death does not see one who views the world in this way.
literal_translation: Just as one would see a little bubble, as one would see a mirage; so the King of Death does not see one who is viewing the world in this manner.

translation: Come, look at this world, adorned like a royal carriage; here fools sink down, but for those who understand, there is no attachment.
literal_translation: Come, look at this world, beautiful like a king's chariot, where fools sink; there is no attachment of the understanding ones.

translation: Whoever was formerly negligent but later is not negligent, illuminates this world like the moon freed from a cloud.
literal_translation: Whoever and previously having been negligent, afterwards he not is negligent, he this world illuminates, from cloud released like moon.

translation: Whose evil deed is superseded by a wholesome one, he illuminates this world like the moon freed from a cloud.
literal_translation: Whose evil action done is covered by a wholesome [deed], he illuminates this world, like the moon released from a cloud.

translation: This world is blind; only a few here see clearly. Like a bird escaped from a net, few go to heaven.
literal_translation: This world is become-blind, a few here see-distinctly; like a bird freed-from-a-net, a few go to heaven.

translation: Swans fly on the path of the sun; they fly through the sky by psychic power. The wise depart from the world, having conquered Mara and his army.
literal_translation: Swans go on the sun's path; they go in the sky by psychic power; the wise are led out from the world, having conquered Mara together with [his] army.

translation: For a person who has transgressed even one rule, who speaks lies, and who has rejected the next world, there is no evil that cannot be done.
literal_translation: For a person having overstepped one teaching, speaking falsely, having rejected the other world, there is not an evil not to be done.

translation: Miserly people indeed do not go to the world of the gods; fools indeed do not praise giving. But a wise person, appreciating giving, because of that alone becomes happy hereafter.
literal_translation: Indeed the miserly do not go to the world of gods; fools truly do not praise generosity; and the wise person, rejoicing in the gift, because of that very thing he becomes happy in the next world.

translation: Better than sole sovereignty over the earth, or going to heaven, or lordship over the entire world, is the fruit of stream-entry.
literal_translation: Than sole sovereignty of the earth, or than going to heaven, than supreme power over the whole world, the fruit of entering the stream is better.

translation: Whose victory is not turned back into defeat, whose victory no one in the world follows—that Buddha of infinite range, the trackless, by what path will you lead him?
literal_translation: Whose victory is not defeated, whose victory no one in the world follows into, that Awakened One of infinite domain, the trackless, by what path will you lead (him)?

translation: In whom there is no craving—the net-like and entangling one—to lead him anywhere, by what track would you lead that Buddha of infinite range, the trackless one?
literal_translation: Of whom the net-like, entangling craving is not anywhere to lead (him) away, that Buddha of infinite range, the trackless one, by what track will you lead him?

translation: Those wise ones intent on meditation, finding delight in the peace of renunciation, even the gods envy them—the Awakened Ones, the mindful.
literal_translation: Who (are) intent on meditation, wise (ones), delighted in the peace of renunciation, even gods for them envy, for (those) awakened (ones), for (those) having mindfulness.

translation: Hard is the birth as a human; hard is the life of mortals; hard is the hearing of the True Teaching; hard is the arising of Buddhas.
literal_translation: Difficult is the gaining of a human state; difficult is the life of mortals; difficult is the hearing of the true teaching; difficult is the arising of Buddhas.

translation: Not to do any evil, to attain the wholesome, and to purify one's own mind: this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
literal_translation: The non-doing of all evil, the undertaking of the wholesome, the purification of one's own mind; this is the instruction of the Buddhas.

translation: Patience is the highest austerity, forbearance; the Buddhas say Nibbāna is supreme. Indeed, one who harms others is not a renunciant, and one who oppresses another is not an ascetic.
literal_translation: Patience is the highest austerity, endurance; the Buddhas say Nibbāna is highest; for one who harms others is not a renunciant, one who harms another is not an ascetic.

translation: Not insulting, not harming, restraint according to the monastic code, moderation in food, dwelling in a secluded place, and devotion to higher meditation—this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
literal_translation: Not blaming, not harming, and restraint in the Patimokkha, and moderation in food, and a secluded dwelling, and devotion in higher mind; this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

translation: Satisfaction is not found in sensual pleasures even by a shower of gold coins. Having understood that sensual pleasures give little enjoyment and are painful, the wise man...
literal_translation: Not by a shower of silver coins satisfaction in sensual pleasures is found; providing little enjoyment and painful are sensual pleasures; thus having understood, the wise man.

translation: Even in heavenly pleasures he finds no delight. The disciple of the perfectly awakened Buddha takes delight only in the destruction of craving.
literal_translation: Even in heavenly sensual pleasures delight he does not find; the disciple of the perfectly awakened Buddha is delighted in the destruction of craving.

translation: Many people, indeed, driven by fear, go for refuge to mountains, forests, parks, trees, and shrines.
literal_translation: Many, indeed, refuge go to, mountains, forests and, parks-trees-shrines, men fear-threatened.

translation: Indeed, this is not a secure refuge, this is not the supreme refuge; not by coming to this refuge is one released from all suffering.
literal_translation: This indeed (is) not a secure refuge, this (is) not the supreme refuge, having come to this refuge, (one) is not released from all suffering.

translation: But whoever has gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Teaching, and the Community, sees with correct wisdom the Four Noble Truths.
literal_translation: Whoever and to the Buddha and to the Teaching and to the Community refuge gone, four noble truths with correct wisdom sees.

translation: Suffering, the origin of suffering, the transcending of suffering, and the noble eightfold path leading to the cessation of suffering.
literal_translation: Suffering, the arising of suffering, and the transcending of suffering, [and] the noble eightfold path leading to the calming of suffering.

translation: This indeed is the safe refuge, this is the supreme refuge; having gone to this refuge, one is freed from all suffering.
literal_translation: This indeed [is] refuge safe, this [is] refuge supreme, this refuge having-come-to, from-all-suffering [one] is-freed.

translation: Rare is a man of noble birth; he is not born everywhere. Wherever such a wise man is born, that family prospers in happiness.
literal_translation: Difficult to find is a thoroughbred man, he not everywhere is born, where he is born, the wise one, that family thrives comfortably.

translation: Happy is the arising of Buddhas, happy is the teaching of the true teaching, happy is the concord of the Sangha, happy is the spiritual practice of those in concord.
literal_translation: Pleasant is the arising of Buddhas, pleasant is the true Dhamma teaching, pleasant is the harmony of the Sangha, pleasant is the practice of those in concord.

translation: Of one honoring those worthy of honor—whether the Buddhas or their disciples—who have transcended mental proliferation and crossed beyond sorrow and lamentation.
literal_translation: Of (one) honoring those worthy of honor, (namely) the Buddhas or indeed the disciples, who have transcended proliferation, who have crossed over sorrow and lamentation.

translation: When someone reveres such as these—those who are emancipated and have no reason to be afraid—no one is able to calculate their merit as being even this much.
literal_translation: Of one revering such ones, (who are) quenched (and) with nothing to fear from anywhere, merit is not possible to be calculated as even just this much by anyone.

translation: Extremely happily indeed we live, free from animosity among those who are hostile; among hostile humans, we dwell free from animosity.
literal_translation: Extremely happily indeed we live, free from animosity among the hostile; among hostile humans, we dwell free from animosity.

translation: We live very happily indeed, healthy among the diseased; among diseased people, we dwell healthy.
literal_translation: Extremely happily indeed we live, among the diseased being healthy, among diseased humans we dwell being healthy.

translation: Extremely happily indeed we live, relaxed among the agitated; among agitated people, we dwell relaxed.
literal_translation: Extremely happily indeed we live, unanxious among the anxious, among anxious people, we dwell unanxious.

translation: Extremely happily indeed we live, we who have nothing at all; we shall be feeders on delight, like the radiant gods.
literal_translation: Very happily indeed we live, of whom for us there is not anything; feeders on delight we shall be, like the radiant gods.

translation: Victory breeds hatred, the defeated live in pain. The peaceful live happily, having abandoned both victory and defeat.
literal_translation: Victory generates hatred, the defeated one lies down in pain; the peaceful one lies down happily, having abandoned victory-and-defeat.

translation: There is no fire like passion, no crime like hatred, no suffering like the aggregates, and no bliss higher than peace.
literal_translation: There is no fire equal to lust; there is no fault equal to hatred; there is no suffering equal to the aggregates; there is no happiness higher than peace.

translation: Hunger is the worst of illnesses, conditioned things are the worst of suffering. Having known this as it truly is, one realizes Nibbana, the highest bliss.
literal_translation: Hunger is the supreme disease, formations are the supreme pain; having known this as it has become, Nibbana is the ultimate happiness.

translation: Health is the highest gain, contentment the highest wealth, trust the highest relative, Nibbāna the highest bliss.
literal_translation: Health-highest are gains, contentment-highest is wealth, trust-highest are kinsmen, Nibbāna is the highest happiness.

translation: Having tasted the flavor of solitude and the flavor of peace, one becomes free from anguish and free from sin while drinking the flavor of joy in the Dhamma.
literal_translation: Having drunk the flavor of solitude and the flavor of peace, he is free from anguish, free from sin, drinking the flavor of joy in the Dhamma.

translation: Seeing the noble ones is good; living with them is always happy. Through not seeing fools, one would always be happy.
literal_translation: Excellent is the seeing of the noble ones; association is always happy; by the not seeing of fools, one would certainly be always happy.

translation: For one who keeps company with fools sorrows for a long time; living with fools is painful, as is being with an enemy always. But a wise person is pleasant to live with, like meeting with relatives.
literal_translation: For one going around associated with fools sorrows a long time; association with fools is painful, like with an enemy always; and the wise man is pleasant to live together with, like a gathering of relatives.

translation: Therefore, one should follow such a person—the wise, the intelligent, the learned, the patient, the devout, and the noble—a good man of great wisdom, just as the moon follows the path of the stars.
literal_translation: Therefore indeed, the wise and the intelligent and the learned, the patient-natured, the devout and noble, that such good man of good wisdom, one should associate with, like the moon the path of the stars.

translation: Engaging oneself in what is unsuitable and not engaging in meditation; having abandoned the goal and grasping after what is dear, one envies those who apply themselves to meditation.
literal_translation: In the unsuitable engaging oneself, and in meditation not engaging, the goal having abandoned, grasping after the dear, one envies the one devoted to meditation.

translation: Do not associate with dear ones, nor ever with those not dear; for it is painful not to see dear ones, and it is painful to see those not dear.
literal_translation: Do not associate with dear ones, [nor] with those not dear ever; the not-seeing of dear ones is painful, and the seeing of those not dear [is painful].

translation: Therefore, do not hold anything dear, for separation from the beloved is painful. No bonds exist for those who have neither dear nor undear.
literal_translation: Therefore, one should not make (anything) dear, for separation from the dear is evil; bonds for them do not exist, for whom there is no dear and undear.

translation: From love arises grief, from love arises fear; for one who is freed from love, there is no grief, how much less fear?
literal_translation: From love arises grief, from love arises fear; for one who is completely released from love, there is no grief, from where [is there] fear?

translation: From love arises grief, from love arises fear; for one who is completely freed from love, there is no grief, much less fear.
literal_translation: From love is born grief, from love is born fear; of one who is freed from love, grief exists not, whence [could there be] fear?

translation: From delight arises grief, from delight arises fear; for one who is freed from delight, there is no grief, let alone fear.
literal_translation: From delight arises grief; from delight arises fear. Of one freed from delight, there is not grief; from where (would there be) fear?

translation: From sensual desire arises sorrow, from sensual desire arises fear; for one who is released from sensual desire, there is no sorrow, much less fear.
literal_translation: From sensual desire arises sorrow, from sensual desire arises fear; for one released from sensual desire, sorrow exists not, whence fear?

translation: From craving arises grief, from craving arises fear. For one who is freed from craving, there is no grief, how much less fear?
literal_translation: From craving arises grief, from craving arises fear; of one freed from craving, there is no grief, from where [is there] fear?

translation: One who is endowed with virtue and insight, established in the Dhamma, a knower of truth, and who fulfills his own duties—him the people hold dear.
literal_translation: Endowed with virtue and insight, established in the Dhamma, knowing truth, doing his own work; that one the people make dear.

translation: One who has developed a wish for the Indescribable, whose mind is permeated with it, and whose heart is not bound to sensual pleasures, is called 'one who flows upstream'.
literal_translation: One whose interest has arisen in the Indescribable, and who would be permeated with the mind, and whose mind is not bound in sensual pleasures, is called 'one who flows upstream'.

translation: When a man who has lived abroad for a long time returns home safely from afar, his relatives, friends, and well-wishers rejoice at his arrival.
literal_translation: A man who has lived abroad for a long time, come safely from afar, relatives, friends and well-wishers rejoice at him who has come.

translation: In the same way, when one who has done merit has gone from this world to the next, their merits receive them, just as relatives welcome a dear one who has returned.
literal_translation: Likewise, even the merit-maker, having gone from this world to the next, merits receive [him], like relatives [welcome] a dear one come [back].

translation: One should give up anger, one should abandon pride, and one should transcend every fetter. Sufferings do not befall that one who does not cling to name and form and possesses nothing.
literal_translation: Anger one should give up, pride one should abandon, every fetter one should transcend; sufferings do not follow that one not clinging to name and form, having nothing.

translation: Whoever restrains flare-up anger like a swerving chariot, that one I call a charioteer; other people are just holding the reins.
literal_translation: Whoever indeed should check arisen anger like a swerving chariot, him I call a charioteer; other person is a rein-holder.

translation: Conquer anger with non-anger, with goodness conquer the bad, conquer the miser with a gift, and with truth the speaker of lies.
literal_translation: By non-anger one should conquer anger, by goodness one should conquer the bad, one should conquer the miser by a gift, by truth the speaker of lies.

translation: Speak the truth, do not get angry, and give when asked even if it is only a little; by these three ways, one may go to the presence of the gods.
literal_translation: One should speak the truth, one should not be angry, one should give a little even when asked; by these three ways, one would go into the presence of the gods.

translation: Those sages who are harmless, always restrained in body, go to the everlasting state, where, having gone, they sorrow no more.
literal_translation: The harmless sages who, always by the body restrained, they go to the everlasting place, where having gone they do not sorrow.

translation: For those who are always watchful, training themselves day and night, and are intent on Nibbāna, their defilements come to an end.
literal_translation: For those always being awake, training day and night, intent on Nibbāna, the defilements go to an end.

translation: This is an ancient thing, Atula, it is not just of today: they blame the one who sits in silence, they blame the one who speaks much, they also blame the one who speaks moderately; there is no one in the world who is not blamed.
literal_translation: This is ancient, Atula, this is not as if it were of today; they blame him sitting silently, they blame him speaking much, they blame even him speaking moderately; there is no one in the world unblamed.

translation: There has never been, there will never be, and there is not now, a person who is solely blamed or solely praised.
literal_translation: Not and there was not, and not will be, not and now exists, exclusively blamed man, exclusively or praised.

translation: If wise people, having investigated, praise him day after day—one of flawless conduct, intelligent, endowed with wisdom and virtue.
literal_translation: If which (one) wise (people) praise, having investigated, tomorrow tomorrow, (one of) flawless behavior, (one) intelligent, (one) wisdom-virtue-endowed.

translation: Like a golden ornament of fine Jambonada gold, who is worthy to criticize him? Even the gods praise him; by Brahma too he is praised.
literal_translation: Like a golden ornament of fine gold, who is worthy to blame that one? Even the gods praise him; by Brahma too he is praised.

translation: One should guard against physical agitation and be restrained in body; abandoning physical misconduct, one should lead a life of good physical conduct.
literal_translation: One should guard against physical agitation, one should be restrained by the body; having abandoned physical misconduct, one should practice good conduct with the body.

translation: One should guard against verbal agitation and be restrained in speech. Abandoning verbal misconduct, one should practice good conduct in speech.
literal_translation: One should guard against verbal agitation; one should be restrained by speech; having abandoned verbal misconduct, one should practice good conduct by speech.

translation: One should guard against mental agitation and be restrained in mind. Having abandoned mental misconduct, one should practice good conduct with the mind.
literal_translation: One should guard against mental disturbance, might be restrained by the mind, having abandoned mental misconduct, one should practice good conduct with the mind.

translation: The wise are restrained in body, and also restrained in speech; the wise are restrained in mind—they are indeed truly well-restrained.
literal_translation: The sages are restrained by body, also restrained by speech, the sages are restrained by mind; they indeed are well-restrained.

translation: You are now like a withered leaf; even the minions of Death have arrived for you. You stand on the threshold of your departure, yet you have no provisions for the journey.
literal_translation: You are now like a yellow leaf; and Death's men are present for you; and you stand at the mouth of departure; and even provision for the journey is not found for you.

translation: Make a refuge for yourself, strive quickly, and be wise. With impurities removed and unblemished, you will reach the divine realm of the Noble Ones.
literal_translation: You make a refuge for yourself, quickly strive, be wise; with stains removed, spotless, to the divine noble-realm you will reach.

translation: And now you are at the end of life, you have set out for the presence of Yama. There is no dwelling for you along the way, nor are provisions for you to be found.
literal_translation: And (at) the end of life now you are, you have gone to (the) presence of Yama, (a) dwelling for you is not along (the) way, and provisions even for you (are) not found.

translation: So, make an island for yourself; strive quickly and be wise. With stains removed and unblemished, you will not come again to birth and old age.
literal_translation: That (you) make an island for yourself; quickly strive, wise be; with removed stains, unblemished, not again birth and old age you will approach.

translation: By degrees, little by little, from moment to moment, a wise man should remove his own impurities, just as a smith removes the dross of silver.
literal_translation: Gradually, the wise man, a little bit a little bit, in moment in moment, (like) a smith indeed of silver, should blow away the impurity of himself.
